title: Machine learning DNA damage response signature and SFN knockdown in cholangiocarcinoma
summary: DNA damage response activity was scored across six intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma cohorts, and 101 combinations of ten machine learning algorithms were compared, with Lasso plus random survival forest selected. The risk model was stable in training and external cohorts, and the core gene SFN was enriched in malignant cells. SFN knockdown suppressed cell proliferation and colony formation, increased cisplatin and gemcitabine sensitivity and raised gamma-H2AX in ICC cell lines. Cohort numbers were not visible in the abstract.
ai_technology: Lasso plus random survival forest, chosen from 101 combined machine learning models
organization: First Affiliated Hospital of Xi’an Jiaotong University

evidence.tested: External validation cohorts plus in vitro SFN knockdown assays in ICC cell lines.
evidence.unknown: Cohort sizes, in vivo effect of SFN and clinical utility; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Builds the prognostic signature and nominates SFN as the gene tested in cells.
